$comment: Files in src/ that intentionally diverge from derive(upstream). Each needs a reason, the upstream SHA it forked from, and the SSOT section it serves.

forks.reason: Find orc-mode by the Claude Code or Codex plugin manifest instead of .cursor-plugin/plugin.json. Drops the model line upstream added, which names a Cursor-only model slug.
Uses harness-local model defaults and classifies provider-qualified model identifiers without Cursor-specific Claude and Gemini fallbacks.

Rewritten as Orc for four harnesses: no Custom Mode, Cursor install, excluded skills, or guide links; adds the attribution line and the mixed-framework check. Lists the orcstack skills (adopt-orcstack, work-brief, adr, contract-inventory, cold-start-review, ci-tiers, test-audit).

Orc description; create-skill, deslop, control-ui/cli, Cursor babysit, Bugbot, Origin, and cloud agents replaced with orcstack routes, surface-check, review-triage, gh, and isolated worktrees. Model invocation is enabled so the SessionStart hook and AGENTS.md routing (ADR-0002 D3) can load it; other skills keep disable-model-invocation. Adds the orcstack gate before routing: one operating rule (stop on another router, route to adopt-orcstack on unconverted artifacts), intent from the Planning SSOT, and a brief per change. Applies project extensions from .orcstack/config.json after the gate (ADR-0004). Links the orcstack verification and records policies (references/verification.md, references/records.md) for the playbooks and skills that are not forked (M3-3, M3-4). Routes to the orcstack knowledge and CI skills (M3-5, M3-6). Reads the SSOT and ADR paths from records in .orcstack/config.json (ADR-0005). The gate also stops on pstack's poteto-mode routing (M3-9 P2). After the gate, work that changes code or documents must open its playbook and copy the steps into the todo before any work, in a governed repository or not (M5-5). Adds orcstack project selection and same-plugin path resolution for coinstalled workflows (§8).
forks.ssot: §3, §4 F1 F6, §6 C1 C5 C7, philosophy §3
